title: How Many Routes Dodge X? | AMC 8-Style Level 4

lines: There are fifty-six ways to walk across this street grid.
Block just one corner, <short pause> and more than half of them vanish!
Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's solve this together, two different ways.
Here's the question.
In this street grid, Mia walks from A to B. She goes only right or up, along the streets of the grid.
She does not go through the corner marked X. How many different routes can she take?
Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
Let's break it down. The grid is five blocks across and three blocks up.
So every route has five right steps and three up steps. That's eight steps in all.
Different routes just put those same eight steps in a different order.
Here's one route Mia could take. It stays away from X.
This route is not allowed, because it passes through X.
We need to count every route that stays away from X.
Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
Welcome back! Let's write a number on every corner: the number of ways Mia can reach it.
Along the bottom street, Mia can only walk right. So each corner there gets a one.
Up the left street, she can only walk up. Each corner there gets a one as well.
Here's the key idea. Mia's last step into a corner comes from the left, or from below.
So add the number on the left and the number below. One plus one is two.
Check it: right then up, or up then right. That's two ways!
Mia can never stand on X, so X gets a zero.
Next to X, zero plus one is one. Then come two and three.
Next row up: one plus two is three. Then three plus zero is three.
Keep going: four, six, and nine.
The top row gives four, seven, eleven, and seventeen.
At B, seventeen plus nine is twenty-six. That's Choice B!
Now for another method. First count EVERY route, then remove the bad ones.
A route is eight steps long, and we only choose which three of them go up.
There are eight choices for the first step that goes up, seven for the second, and six for the third.
But the same three steps get picked in six different orders. So divide by six.
Three hundred thirty-six over six is fifty-six routes in all.
Now the bad routes, the ones through X.
From A to X is two rights and one up. The up step can be first, second, or third.
That's three ways. From X to B is three rights and two ups.
Pick two of those five steps to go up. Five times four is twenty, and each pair is counted twice.
So that's ten ways to finish. Each of the three starts goes with each of the ten finishes.
Why multiply? Every start can be paired with every finish.
Three times ten is thirty routes through X. Fifty-six minus thirty is twenty-six. It matches!
So when would you pick each way? Corner numbers work even with lots of blocked corners.
Subtracting is the fastest when just one corner is blocked.
Choice C, thirty, counts every route that goes THROUGH X. Those are the ones to take away!
Choice E, fifty-six, counts every route, and forgets about X.
Thirty-five is what you'd get if you counted the grid as only four blocks wide.
Twenty is what a grid three blocks wide would give.
Watch out: don't add three and ten here. Fifty-six minus thirteen is forty-three, and that's not a choice.
So here's a great habit: count the blocks carefully, and check which routes you were asked for.

scenes.chapter: Your turn: a four by four grid
lines: Ready for a challenge? Now the grid is four blocks across and four blocks up.
Corner X is right in the middle. How many routes go from A to B without passing X?
Pause the video, and go for it!
Let's solve it by subtracting. Every route has four rights and four ups.
Eight times seven times six times five, over four times three times two times one, is seventy.
Pick which two of the four steps go up: four times three is twelve, and each pair is counted twice, so six ways.
From X to B is six ways too. So six times six is thirty-six routes through X.
Seventy minus thirty-six is thirty-four!
In the corner table, the zero in the middle wipes out every route through X.
The corner numbers give thirty-four as well. If you found it, amazing work!
Here's the big idea to remember.
Count all the routes, then subtract the routes through the blocked corner.
Or fill in corner numbers: add the left and below, with a zero on the blocked corner.
I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
